issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Improve page style isolation for public-facing pages so page styles stay contained and do not accidentally affect other areas of the site.

Background

Several pages were still relying on broader styling behavior. This makes future design changes riskier because a style update in one page can unexpectedly change another page or layout.

Expected behavior

  • Keep page-specific styles scoped to the owning page.
  • Preserve the current visual appearance of the affected pages.
  • Avoid unexpected style changes in shared layouts or other pages.
  • Make future page styling updates easier to review and maintain.

Notes

This should keep the public page design unchanged while reducing the chance of styling side effects.

issues.display_title: Issue #1721: [Linting] Separate ESLint rules by project area
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

The project currently applies the same linting setup to Angular application code, unit tests, the server, and end-to-end tests. These areas run in different environments and should not be checked as if they were all Angular components.

This task will organize the linting setup so each area receives checks that are relevant to its purpose. This will make lint results easier to understand and reduce unrelated warnings.

Scope

  • Separate linting coverage for Angular application code, unit tests, server-side code, end-to-end tests, and HTML templates.
  • Keep the current linting standards and severity levels unchanged.
  • Keep inline and external Angular templates covered.
  • Preserve existing lint commands.
  • Document the lint result before and after the change.

Acceptance criteria

  • Angular-specific checks apply only to Angular source and relevant tests.
  • Server-side and end-to-end test files no longer receive component-specific Angular checks.
  • Angular templates continue to receive recommended accessibility checks.
  • Unit tests have a clearly defined linting scope.
  • The lint command runs without configuration, parser, or processor errors.
  • Any change in the number of findings is documented.
  • No application behavior or production source is changed to complete this task.

Out of scope

  • Fixing the existing lint findings.
  • Changing rule severity.
  • Adding stricter type-aware checks.
  • Replacing formatting rules.
  • Adding a CI quality gate.

Verification

Run the project lint command and confirm representative application, template, unit-test, server, and end-to-end files receive the intended checks. Existing code-quality findings may remain; configuration errors may not.

issues.display_title: Issue #1722: [Linting] Move code formatting away from deprecated ESLint rules
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Several formatting checks used by the project are deprecated and will be removed from a future ESLint release. Formatting should be moved to a maintained tool while ESLint remains focused on code quality and Angular correctness.

This task should choose one consistent formatting approach for the repository and avoid creating competing sources of truth.

Scope

  • Adopt a maintained formatter or maintained formatting rule set.
  • Preserve the project's current style as closely as practical.
  • Remove deprecated formatting responsibilities from the current ESLint setup.
  • Add convenient commands for checking and applying formatting.
  • Document the chosen workflow for contributors.

Acceptance criteria

  • Deprecated ESLint formatting rules are no longer used.
  • TypeScript, HTML, SCSS, JSON, and Markdown have a clear formatting workflow where applicable.
  • Existing formatting conventions are preserved unless an intentional change is documented.
  • Formatting and code-quality checks do not conflict.
  • Contributors can check formatting without changing files.
  • Contributors can apply formatting with one documented command.
  • The application build remains successful.

Out of scope

  • Fixing unrelated lint errors.
  • Introducing stricter application rules.
  • Large-scale code cleanup unrelated to formatting.

Dependency

Complete the lint-scope cleanup first so formatting behavior can be introduced on a stable configuration.

issues.display_title: Issue #1723: [Linting] Resolve TypeScript quality findings in shared components
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Shared components currently contain a concentrated set of TypeScript lint findings. Because these components are reused across the application, cleaning them up first will improve consistency and reduce repeated risk for future feature work.

The current audit found 22 affected component files with 68 errors and 71 warnings. Common themes include loose types, equality checks, unused code, output naming, selectors, and empty lifecycle methods.

Scope

  • Resolve TypeScript lint findings under the shared components area.
  • Replace loose or unclear types with meaningful types where practical.
  • Remove genuinely unused code.
  • Correct equality checks without changing intended behavior.
  • Update Angular component API conventions carefully and update all call sites when required.
  • Add or update focused tests for behavior-sensitive changes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Shared component TypeScript files have no lint errors.
  • Remaining warnings, if any, are explicitly justified and narrowly suppressed.
  • Public component inputs and outputs continue to work at every call site.
  • No blanket rule disabling is added.
  • Relevant unit tests pass.
  • The Angular development build succeeds.
  • Any intentional behavior change is documented.

Out of scope

  • Template accessibility findings, which are tracked separately.
  • Page-level and shared-service findings.
  • General lint configuration changes.

Notes

Output renaming and selector changes can affect many templates. Treat these as compatibility changes, search all usages, and verify the affected flows.

issues.display_title: Issue #1724: [Linting] Resolve TypeScript quality findings in pages and feature areas
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Page and feature code contains the largest share of the current TypeScript lint backlog. The audit found 85 affected files with 423 errors and 673 warnings.

This work should be delivered incrementally by feature area so changes remain reviewable and can be tested without mixing unrelated user flows.

Scope

  • Resolve TypeScript lint findings under the pages and feature areas.
  • Prioritize unsafe or correctness-related findings before style warnings.
  • Replace loose types progressively with meaningful domain types.
  • Remove unused code and correct equality checks.
  • Preserve user-visible behavior.
  • Split delivery into small pull requests grouped by feature or route.

Suggested delivery order

  1. Small and low-risk pages.
  2. Settings and account flows.
  3. Pricing and payment flows.
  4. Gallery management flows.
  5. Virtual gallery editor areas.

Acceptance criteria

  • Each completed feature area has no TypeScript lint errors.
  • The final pages area has no TypeScript lint errors.
  • Remaining warnings, if any, are documented and narrowly justified.
  • No blanket rule disabling is introduced.
  • Behavior-sensitive changes include appropriate tests.
  • Affected user flows are smoke-tested.
  • The Angular development build succeeds after each pull request.

Out of scope

  • Shared components and shared services.
  • Template accessibility findings.
  • Lint configuration or severity changes.

Notes

This is intentionally one roadmap issue with multiple small pull requests. Avoid a single repository-wide cleanup pull request.

issues.display_title: Issue #1726: [Linting] Align Angular component APIs with current conventions
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

The lint audit identified Angular-specific issues such as event outputs using the "on" prefix, components without the project selector prefix, and empty lifecycle methods.

These findings affect the consistency and maintainability of component APIs. Some fixes may touch multiple consumers, so they should be handled as deliberate compatibility updates rather than mechanical renames.

Scope

  • Rename event outputs that do not follow Angular conventions.
  • Align component selectors with the project's naming convention where practical.
  • Remove empty lifecycle methods and unnecessary lifecycle declarations.
  • Update every affected template and TypeScript consumer.
  • Preserve public behavior and emitted event semantics.

Acceptance criteria

  • Angular-specific TypeScript lint errors are resolved.
  • All renamed outputs and selectors are updated at every call site.
  • Components continue to emit the same data at the same user interactions.
  • Empty lifecycle methods are removed unless a documented reason requires them.
  • No broad lint suppression is added.
  • Relevant unit tests pass.
  • The Angular development build succeeds.
  • Affected UI flows are smoke-tested.

Out of scope

  • General TypeScript cleanup unrelated to Angular APIs.
  • Template accessibility findings.
  • Lint configuration changes.

Notes

Coordinate this task with the area-based cleanup issues to avoid duplicate edits. If an API is already corrected in an area cleanup, record it here instead of changing it twice.

issues.display_title: Issue #1727: [Accessibility] Resolve Angular template lint findings
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

The lint audit found 169 accessibility-related errors across Angular templates. The largest groups involve labels that are not connected to controls, mouse interactions without keyboard support, interactive elements that cannot receive focus, and images without alternative text.

These are user-facing accessibility gaps and should be fixed based on the intended interaction, not by silencing the checks.

Scope

  • Associate form labels with the correct controls.
  • Ensure custom clickable elements are keyboard accessible or replace them with native controls.
  • Ensure interactive elements can receive focus.
  • Add meaningful alternative text or correctly mark decorative images.
  • Review affected interactions for accessible names, roles, and states.
  • Add focused tests where interaction behavior changes.

Acceptance criteria

  • Angular HTML templates have no accessibility lint errors.
  • Form controls have correctly associated labels or accessible names.
  • Every interactive action can be completed with a keyboard.
  • Focus behavior is visible and logical.
  • Images have appropriate alternative text treatment.
  • Native HTML elements are preferred where they provide the required behavior.
  • No blanket accessibility-rule suppression is added.
  • Affected flows are keyboard smoke-tested.
  • The Angular development build succeeds.

Out of scope

  • Visual redesign.
  • General TypeScript lint cleanup.
  • Changing the accessibility rule set to hide existing findings.

issues.display_title: Issue #1728: [Linting] Enable type-aware checks and enforce linting in CI
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Final step of the linting roadmap: enable deeper TypeScript checks and make linting an automated local quality gate.

Delivered: a Husky + lint-staged pre-commit gate and a defined, zero-error set of type-aware ESLint rules. The no-unsafe-* family and two promise rules were measured and deferred; their figures are retained below for follow-up.

Decision: no GitHub Actions (29 July 2026)

GitHub Actions is not used in this repository. The local pre-commit gate is the intended enforcement point.

Known trade-offs:

  • It can be bypassed with git commit --no-verify.
  • It validates staged files rather than the whole repository.
  • It cannot be a protected-branch requirement.
  • It fixes and restages eligible files using eslint --fix and prettier --write.

Whole-repository checks remain manual: pnpm lint and pnpm format:check.

Delivered work

PR Change
#1741 Husky + lint-staged pre-commit hook; excluded qa_testing/ from ESLint; removed dead @types/jasminewd2
#1742 Enabled projectService, await-thenable, no-base-to-string, no-redundant-type-constituents, no-unnecessary-type-assertion, and only-throw-error
#1743 Enabled require-await
#1744 Deliberately disabled no-explicit-any
#1745 Enabled no-misused-promises

The intended baseline is 0 lint errors and 8 documented no-console warnings.

Enforced type-aware rules

await-thenable, no-misused-promises, no-base-to-string, no-redundant-type-constituents, no-unnecessary-type-assertion, only-throw-error, and require-await.

Bugs fixed during delivery

  • Prevented silently pending uploads when building an exhibition-uploader payload fails.
  • Prevented promocode-form from leaving isFetching stuck after async initialization fails.
  • Routed rejections from async subscribe callbacks to their request-failure handlers.
  • Preserved HttpErrorResponse prototype behavior in the data interceptor.
  • Removed invalid await use on a synchronous editor value.
  • Removed obsolete Jasmine typing declarations that produced phantom findings.

Acceptance criteria

  • Defined type-aware lint rules are enabled and clear.
  • Enabled-rule findings are resolved or have a scoped reason.
  • Local lint reports 0 errors.
  • Staged files run linting and formatting through the pre-commit hook.
  • Repository-wide commands are documented.
  • Development build succeeds.

Deferred work

no-floating-promises 189 Requires per-site decisions
prefer-promise-reject-errors 62 Mechanical follow-up
no-console 8 Debug logging baseline

Out of scope

  • Framework upgrades.
  • Whole-repository formatting changes.
  • GitHub Actions or PR/push-triggered checks.

issues.display_title: Issue #1747: [Editor] Artwork detail panel labels render dark on dark background
issues.main_description_html:
Description

In the Artwork detail panel of the editor (Artworks tab → select an artwork), several text elements render in a dark or near-black color on the dark panel background. Contrast is so low that the labels are barely readable.

Affected text

Element Location

Scaling scaling-image.component.html
Grid Align section (app-align-object)
Bottom / Top Align section (app-align-object)

Other labels in the same panel (Your Text:, Link:, and Email:) render in a readable light gray, so the styling is inconsistent within the panel.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the editor of any virtual gallery.
  2. Go to the Artworks tab.
  3. Select an artwork to open its detail panel.

All labels in the artwork detail panel use the same light foreground color as the editor sidebar and meet the WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast ratio against the dark panel background.

The listed labels render dark on dark and are difficult to read.
